assessment: Using zebrafish as an in vivo model, this study reveals for the first time that mutations in the kinesin light chain gene klc4, which are known to cause a form of early onset hereditary spastic paraplegia in human, affect specific aspects of neuronal development and nervous system functions. High-resolution movies of developing sensory neurons in vivo and behavioral assays support the key findings that the motor subunit Klc4 plays essential functions in the control of neuronal morphogenesis and compartmentalization as well as associated behaviors.
